note: Layer 6 — scorecard coupling. Measures whether the per-dimension scorecard tracks the source it scores, in BOTH directions: repeatability (same source => same score) and sensitivity (changed source => moved score). Every other eval layer measures a judgment (flag/no-flag, approve/reject, replay equivalence); the scorecard numbers are the skill's headline output and were unmeasured. attempt 0 in each probe is OBSERVATIONAL — harvested from production runs, not a designed replication — and is seeded so the layer starts from real evidence rather than an empty file. Controlled attempts (>= 1) must pin skill_rev, which G19 records as of the commit that added this layer.

prereg.repeatability: N >= 3 independent Critic passes over one corpus at a pinned source SHA, fresh context each, no prior artifacts on disk, skill_rev pinned and identical across attempts. Report per-dimension mean, spread, and max pairwise gap. PREDICTION: max pairwise gap <= 1.0 on every dimension. The observational attempt 0 measured 3.0, so a controlled run reproducing >= 2.0 CONFIRMS the defect rather than refuting the design.
prereg.sensitivity: Critic passes immediately before and after a commit known to resolve a Serious-or-worse structural finding, same skill_rev, same corpus otherwise. PREDICTION: the dimension the finding was filed under moves UP. attempt 0 measured seven consecutive Serious resolutions with zero UP deltas across nine dimensions and eleven loops.
prereg.interpretation: The two probes fail in opposite directions and a fix for one can worsen the other: tightening anchors to raise repeatability can flatten sensitivity, and vice versa. Neither number alone licenses a rubric change — 2b (a value-domain gate on off-anchor scores) is explicitly gated on BOTH reading out.
prereg.variance_collapse: REGISTERED 2026-08-06, BEFORE passes 4-6 of either arm were dispatched (commit precedes results). Follows up attempt 2's largest post-hoc observation: a high prior barely moved the mean (+0.833) but appeared to collapse inter-rater spread (HIGH pass means spread 0.222, sample SD 0.116; BLIND spread 1.222, sample SD 0.663). At N=3 a variance estimate is nearly worthless, which is the whole reason for this attempt. Design: extend BLIND and HIGH to N=6 each by adding three passes per arm; passes 1-3 are attempt 1's and attempt 2's, reused unchanged. Same pinned SHA 1bdec1a, same skill_rev 23bea47, same model, same harness files verified by hash (blind da50691b5db54f4d, primed 89067a55ab63fecc) and the same deterministically regenerated 809-byte prime at mean 9.278. LOW is NOT extended: the claim under test is HIGH-vs-BLIND, and LOW's N=3 spread of 1.389 already sits at BLIND's level. PRIMARY TEST: F = sample_var(BLIND) / sample_var(HIGH) on the six per-pass grand means, df (5,5). CONFIRMED if F >= 5.05, the one-tailed alpha=0.05 critical value. PREDICTION: HIGH's SD will RISE from 0.116 — an SD that tight off three draws is implausible and regression to the mean is expected — but the ratio will still clear 5.05. REFUTED if F < 5.05, which can happen two ways worth distinguishing in the writeup: HIGH's spread widening toward BLIND's, or BLIND's spread narrowing because its pass B was an outlier. SECONDARY, descriptive only: raw spread (max-min) per arm, and a robust median-absolute-deviation comparison, since the F-test assumes normality and at N=6 is low-powered and outlier-sensitive. Every pass is recorded including any that fails to return valid JSON, with a reason; the Layer-3 no-silent-exclusion contract applies.
prereg.ratchet: REGISTERED 2026-08-06, BEFORE the arms were dispatched (commit precedes results). Third probe, added because attempt 1's blind_vs_history adjunct measured a 1.685 gap larger than the 1.22 repeatability noise floor. Question: does a prior SCORE move a Critic's judgment of unchanged source? Design: identical lean harness, identical corpus at source_rev 1bdec1a, identical skill_rev 23bea47; the two primed arms differ from each other by the corpus path alone and from the blind arm only by title, path and the prior-review block (verified by generating the harnesses from the blind one). Each primed corpus carries ONE terse CURRENT_REVIEW.json holding nine scores and no proof prose — priming with production's own justifications would vary the numbers and the argument for them at once, and only the numbers are the manipulation. Arm HIGH primes with the real production scorecard (mean 9.278, +1.685 vs the blind 7.593). Arm LOW primes with those same scores displaced down 3.5 and clamped to the half-point grid (mean 5.778, -1.815), preserving relative shape so data_flow stays lowest. N=3 per arm. G8 is DELIBERATELY INERT and the harness says so in as many words ('you are not bound by the prior review'), so any displacement observed is anchoring alone rather than a rule forbidding an increase; with G8 active the effect could only be larger, making this the conservative direction. PREDICTIONS: (1) ANCHORING CONFIRMED if BOTH arm grand means displace toward their prime by >= 1.0 — that is ~2.6 standard errors, given the blind arm's measured per-pass SD of 0.66 over N=3. (2) PARTIAL / prior-carries-information if HIGH rises >= 1.0 but LOW does not fall >= 1.0: a Critic that follows a prior upward but refuses a wrong prior downward is reading evidence, not anchoring. (3) REFUTED if neither arm displaces >= 1.0, in which case the production-vs-blind gap must be explained by the three recorded confounds instead. Falsifiability rests on arm LOW: without it, 'production scored higher because history documented real improvement' survives every result.

per_dimension.note: Controlled attempt 1, repeatability probe. mean and max_pairwise_gap over N=3 blind Critic passes at source_rev 1bdec1a, skill_rev 23bea47. These are the measured noise floors per dimension.

attempts.source: Two production runs against one C#/UWP repo. Run B began at Run A's HEAD, so both scorecards describe the same source, at most one loop's refactor apart. Score Anchors were byte-identical: references/architecture-rubric-scoring.md has exactly one commit in its history and was untouched between the runs. Other skill files DID change between them, which is why this is observational and not controlled.
attempts.finding: The aggregate is stable (averages agree to 0.22) while per-dimension attribution is close to arbitrary. test_strategy — the HALT_SUCCESS bar — was certified 9.5 by one Critic and 6.5 by the next on the same code. No single loop's refactor raises domain_modeling 3.0 while lowering test_strategy 3.0.

attempts.source: A 15-loop production run of this skill against its own repo, loops 4-14.
attempts.finding: Seven Serious structural defects in the validator, the gates and the routing were resolved across eleven consecutive loops, and the scorecard produced zero UP deltas on any of nine dimensions. Same source => different scores (repeatability probe); different source => same scores (this probe). Both are failures of the same coupling.

attempts.corpus: steamgriddb-xbox (C#/UWP Game Bar widget), 58 C#/XAML files, ~429k chars, pinned in a detached git worktree outside the repo root. Stack lens fixed to lens-generic.md (the 'Anything else' row) so lens choice could not become a confound.
attempts.model: session default (Opus 5) for all three passes; subagent_type general-purpose; byte-identical dispatch prompts pointing at one on-disk harness spec.
attempts.prereg_verdict: PREDICTION REFUTED (max gap 2.0 > 1.0); CONFIRM-DEFECT BAR MET (>= 2.0). The scorecard is not per-dimension repeatable at this skill_rev.
attempts.finding: The defect reproduces under control, but its STRUCTURE is not what attempt 0 suggested and attempt 0's headline does not survive. Attempt 0 read as compensating per-dimension swings around a stable average (mean shift 0.22 while individual dimensions moved 3.0). Attempt 1 is the opposite shape: pass B scored strictly lower than BOTH other passes on 9 of 9 dimensions — a uniform rater-severity offset — while passes A and C were identical on 7 of 9 (mean absolute difference 0.167). The aggregate was therefore NOT stable here: pass means spread 1.222, five times attempt 0's 0.22. Per-dimension ATTRIBUTION is substantially reproducible; overall SEVERITY calibration is what drifts, and it drags every dimension together.
attempts.caveat: N=3 with a single deviant rater cannot distinguish a two-mode distribution from one draw off a wide continuum. The 'uniform offset' claim describes this sample; it is not established as the population shape. A higher-N attempt is the way to settle it.
attempts.adjunct_finding: Independent of the probe: all three blind passes converged on the SAME structural defects in prose (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs at 1987 lines as the ceiling, the 'Unknown' string sentinel threaded across modules, StoreNameLookup's unlocked Dictionary reads outside its own gates, CancellationToken plumbed through SteamGridDbClient and supplied by no caller, LibraryOperationGuard.TryBegin's non-atomic check-then-set, the untested session guard at PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:1442, the dead InverseBooleanToVisibilityConverter). The FINDINGS repeat; only the NUMBERS do not. That is the skill's own unifying thesis measured directly: structured, source-anchored claims reproduce, free-form scalar judgment does not.
deviations: Lean scoring harness: validation.md and the output-format trio were NOT loaded (~33k tokens/pass). G4, G5 and G6 were inlined verbatim so score-shaping pressure was preserved; G8 is inert with no history. This measures a Critic that scores under the anchors but emits no protocol artifact.

Build and tests were not re-run per pass. 'Build passes; 206 tests passing' was supplied identically to all three passes, so it cannot be a source of variance, but credibility was therefore scored on structure rather than on an observed run.

Five artifact files (CURRENT_REVIEW.{json,md}, REVIEW_HISTORY.{json,md}, findings_registry.json) are TRACKED in the target repo and materialized in the pinned worktree. They were deleted to satisfy the no-prior-artifacts requirement; `git status` in the corpus consequently showed five deletions, which the harness disclosed as setup rather than as a finding.
PURGE_LOG.jsonl was retained. It carries no scores but discloses that a prior 15-loop run ended HALT_LOOP_CAP. Constant across all three passes.
CODE-REVIEW.md was retained: a genuine 2026-08-03 developer document (commit fd90da6) carrying no scorecard, and part of the real corpus.

attempts.note: Not a pre-registered probe. Falls out for free from attempt 1: the production Run C loop-15 terminal scorecard describes this exact SHA, and was produced by a Critic WITH REVIEW_HISTORY.json, findings_registry.json and its own prior scorecard on disk.
attempts.finding: On identical source, a Critic holding its own history scored 1.69 higher than the mean of three blind Critics, and exceeded EVERY blind pass on 8 of 9 dimensions. data_flow (7.5) is the sole dimension where production and blind agree — and it is the one dimension production never ratcheted. This is consistent with the ratchet hypothesis: G8 blocks unproven INCREASES but nothing re-baselines a score downward, so fifteen individually-justified upward steps compound.
attempts.caveat: NOT a controlled test of the ratchet. Confounded at least three ways: the production Critic ran the full protocol including the emit gates this harness omits; it had a findings registry supplying candidate evidence; and it re-ran the build itself. Establishing the ratchet needs its own design, and this entry is recorded as a lead, not a result.
attempts.superseded_by: attempt 2 (probe: ratchet) tested this causally. The 1.685 gap is NOT reproduced by priming alone: a prior score displaces a Critic by at most 0.833. Most of the production/blind gap is therefore still unexplained and is likely the confounds above.

attempts.design: Three arms at one SHA. BLIND is attempt 1's data reused unchanged. HIGH and LOW each got one terse CURRENT_REVIEW.json holding nine scores and no proof prose. The two primed harnesses were GENERATED from the blind harness and verified to differ from each other by the corpus path alone (2 diff lines) and from blind only by title, path and the prior-review block. G8 was deliberately inert and the harness said so outright ('you are not bound by the prior review'), making this the conservative direction: with G8 active the effect could only be larger.
attempts.prereg_verdict: REFUTED. The registered bar was a >= 1.0 grand-mean displacement toward the prime in BOTH arms. HIGH reached +0.833, LOW only -0.296; neither cleared it, so outcome (3) applies as written. Anchoring at the strength predicted is not established, and the 1.685 production-vs-blind gap is NOT reproduced by priming alone — most of it remains attributable to the three recorded confounds.

post_hoc.warning: Everything in this block is POST HOC and was not registered. It is recorded because it is systematic, not because it rescues the prediction. The pre-registered verdict above stands unchanged.
post_hoc.direction: Both arms moved TOWARD their prime, neither away. HIGH rose on 9/9 dimensions; LOW fell on 7/9.
post_hoc.partial_adjustment: Per dimension, the HIGH arm consistently closed 40-55% of the gap between the blind score and the prime, and the size of the move tracked the size of the gap available: state_management (gap 2.33) +1.17, simplicity (2.50) +1.33, credibility (2.17) +1.17, concurrency (2.17) +1.17, domain_modeling (2.33) +0.83, framework_idioms (1.67) +0.67, architecture_quality (1.00) +0.67, test_strategy (0.83) +0.33. The internal control is data_flow, the one dimension whose prime (7.5) essentially equalled the blind value (7.33): it moved +0.17. A dimension with no room to move did not move.
post_hoc.asymmetry: The upward pull was 2.81x the downward pull (+0.833 vs -0.296; 49% vs 16% of available gap). Directionally consistent with the ratchet claim — priors pull up far harder than down — but the magnitudes are below the registered bar.
post_hoc.variance_collapse: The clearest effect was not on the mean. HIGH-arm pass means were 8.333/8.556/8.389, a spread of 0.222 (sd 0.094), against blind's 1.222 (sd 0.541) and LOW's 1.389 (sd 0.585). A high prior made three independent Critics agree with each other roughly six times more tightly. If that holds up, a prior scorecard buys apparent repeatability without buying accuracy — which would make a converging run's stability partly an artifact of its own history. At N=3 a variance ratio is very unstable; this needs a higher-N attempt before it is claimed.
post_hoc.threshold_was_wrong: The registered metric — absolute grand-mean displacement — averages across dimensions whose available gap ranges from 0.17 to 2.50, so it cannot distinguish 'did not anchor' from 'had nowhere to go'. Fraction-of-available-gap is the better statistic and is registered here for any future attempt. Switching metrics after seeing the data would be exactly the move this layer exists to prevent, so it is NOT applied to this attempt's verdict.

attempts.behavioral_observation: One LOW-arm pass (L1) volunteered that it 'read the prior review only after my independent scorecard was written'. It scored 7.889 — the closest of any primed pass to the blind grand mean of 7.593, and 1.389 above its own arm's lowest pass. Self-blinding was invented by one rater unprompted and appears to have worked. That is a cheap candidate mitigation (score first, read the prior only to compute the delta) and it needs its own attempt before it is believed off a single observation.
attempts.superseded_in_part_by: attempt 3 re-ran both arms at N=6. The +0.833 displacement settles to +0.759 — the >= 1.0 bar is still not met, so this REFUTED verdict stands on twice the data. The variance collapse survives at reduced size. The band-unlock finding in attempt 3 is the sharper statement of what a prior actually does.
deviations: Inherits every deviation of attempt 1's lean harness: validation.md and the output-format trio not loaded, G4/G5/G6 inlined, build/test state supplied rather than run.

The primed prior carries nine scores and NO proof prose. This isolates the number from the argument for it, but it is therefore not a replica of production, where the prior arrives with justifications, a findings registry and a 15-loop history.
The BLIND arm was not re-run; attempt 1's three passes are reused. Same harness, same SHA, same skill_rev, same model, ~40 minutes earlier.

attempts.design: BLIND and HIGH each extended from 3 to 6 passes. Passes 1-3 reused from attempts 1 and 2; passes 4-6 dispatched fresh against rebuilt worktrees at the same SHA, with the harness files verified unchanged by hash (blind da50691b5db54f4d, primed 89067a55ab63fecc) and the 809-byte prime regenerated deterministically to the same mean 9.278. LOW not extended.
attempts.prereg_verdict: CONFIRMED, but marginally. F = 5.538 against the registered critical value of 5.050 (p = 0.0418). A high prior does reduce inter-rater variance on identical source. The registered PREDICTION also held in both directions: HIGH's SD rose from the implausibly tight N=3 value of 0.116 to 0.196 exactly as regression to the mean predicts, and BLIND's fell from 0.663 to 0.460 — so the true effect is roughly half what N=3 suggested (SD ratio 5.7x -> 2.35x), and it still clears the bar.
attempts.honest_qualification: This is weak evidence and must not be reported as more. p = 0.0418 with n=6 per arm on a single pre-registered test is one modest study, and the REGISTERED SECONDARY robust check DISAGREES: Brown-Forsythe on absolute deviations from the median gives t(10) = 1.797 against a 2.228 critical value — not significant. The F-test assumes normality and is outlier-sensitive at this n; blind pass B2 (6.833) is doing real work in the numerator. Supporting but not decisive: HIGH's spread is smaller than BLIND's on 7 of 9 dimensions, the exceptions being framework_idioms (HIGH wider, 1.5 vs 0.5) and simplicity (tied at 1.5). N=10-12 per arm would settle it.

ratchet_restated_at_n6.note: Attempt 2's registered >= 1.0 bar is still not met, now on twice the data. That REFUTED verdict is firmer, not weaker: a prior score does not move the mean as much as the production-vs-blind gap implied.

post_hoc_band_unlock.warning: POST HOC and not registered. The 9.0 cutpoint is a rubric anchor rather than a fitted threshold, but it was chosen after seeing the data and needs its own pre-registration before it is claimed as established.
post_hoc_band_unlock.finding: This is the cleanest signal in the layer and it reframes the mechanism. Across 54 scores from six independent blind Critics, NOT ONE exceeded 8.5. Primed Critics emitted 15 scores at 9.0 or above and reached 9.5 three times, with 5 of 6 passes crossing 9.0. A prior does not nudge scores upward by a constant — it removes a CEILING. The blind rater will not enter a scoring band on this evidence that the primed rater enters routinely.
post_hoc_band_unlock.why_it_matters: Every gate that certifies convergence lives above the blind ceiling. G5's residual requirement triggers at 9.5, G6 at 10, and G21's HALT_SUCCESS bar sits at 9.5 across the board. On this corpus at this skill_rev, a Critic reading no prior scorecard CANNOT reach HALT_SUCCESS at all — its ceiling is 8.5 — while a Critic reading its own prior scorecard can. Certification would then be partly a function of having certified before. Note the limit honestly: the >= 9.5 comparison on its own is NOT significant (3 occurrences, p = 0.121), so the band-unlock is established at 9.0 and only suggested at the gate threshold itself.
post_hoc_band_unlock.scope: RESOLVED by attempt 4 without further sampling: the 8.5 ceiling is corpus-specific, not a rubric property. What survives is the narrower and more relevant claim that no blind pass on either corpus reached 9.5.

deviations: Inherits every deviation of the lean harness used throughout this layer.
Passes 1-3 of each arm were run earlier in the session than passes 4-6; identical harness hash, corpus SHA, skill_rev and model, but not the same wall-clock window.

A commit (9425b54) landed on the target repo's master between the two batches. Both batches read detached worktrees pinned to 1bdec1a and the primed scorecard was verified byte-equal to the artifact at that SHA, so the corpus was unaffected.

attempts.note: Answers attempt 3's open question at no cost. Loop 1 of an archived run IS a blind Critic pass whenever no prior REVIEW_HISTORY existed on disk when it ran, so the archives already held the second-corpus evidence a fresh probe would have bought. Recorded because the cheap answer arrived after the expensive one and the record should show that.
attempts.classification: Run A loop 1 and Run S loop 1 qualify as blind (nothing prior on disk). Run B loop 1 qualifies: Run A's history had been purged to .contest-refactor-backup-20260805-000130 before it ran. Run C loop 1 does NOT qualify — the combined history file carries loop numbers [1..10, 1..15], so Run C's loop 1 was appended after Run B's ten and that Critic could read a prior scorecard for the same codebase. It is reported here as primed.
attempts.finding: Two results, and they split the attempt-3 question. FIRST: the 8.5 ceiling is CORPUS-SPECIFIC, not a property of the rubric. A blind Critic over agent-skills (Python, stdlib-only) emitted 9.0 on four of nine dimensions immediately, so 'no blind Critic ever scores above 8.5' is a fact about the steamgriddb codebase, not about the scoring instrument. Attempt 3's stronger reading is refuted. SECOND, and what survives: across 81 blind scores from nine passes, two corpora and at least three skill revisions, NOT ONE reached 9.5 — the threshold G5's residual requirement, G6's 10-anchor and G21's HALT_SUCCESS bar all certify against.
attempts.natural_experiment: Run B loop 1 versus Run C loop 1 is the sharpest pair in the archive and it addresses exactly what attempt 3 could not establish. Run C began at Run B's HEAD, so the two describe the same codebase at most one loop's refactor apart. Run B's loop 1 was blind: max 8.5, nothing at 9.0 or above. Run C's loop 1 was primed with Run B's ten loops: max 9.5, with THREE dimensions at 9.5 (domain_modeling, framework_idioms, credibility). Near-identical source, one blind and one primed, and only the primed pass crosses the gate threshold — on three dimensions at once, in its first loop, before touching a line of code.
caveats: Observational, n=1 per archived run, and not a designed replication.

The archived passes ran the FULL protocol (validation.md and the emit gates, which exert pressure toward 9.5 via G5/G21) at different skill revisions, unlike the lean harness used in attempts 1-3. That heterogeneity strengthens the 9.5 claim — more rulesets, still no 9.5 — while weakening any per-pass comparison.

skill_rev is null in every archived artifact because the field did not exist yet. This is precisely the attribution gap Change 1 was added to close, and it is why the Run B / Run C pair is suggestive rather than clean: 29 skill commits also separate them.
The steamgriddb blind pool is dominated by attempts 1-3 (54 of 72 scores); only 18 come from full-protocol runs.
Run S is the skill reviewing its own repository, which carries its own bias direction and is the only source of every blind score at or above 9.0.

attempts.status: complete — RE-ANALYSIS of attempts 1-3, zero new sampling
attempts.note: No new passes. Attempts 1-3 analysed a 9-dimension x 6-rater design with raw spread, sample SD and an F-test on grand means, which collapses each rater to one number and discards the structure that decides the practical question. The standard analysis for repeated ratings of the same targets on a continuous scale is a two-way variance decomposition plus the intraclass correlation. Running it on the data already collected changed the recommendation set, so it is recorded as its own attempt rather than folded silently into attempt 3.

icc.reading: ICC(2,1) is absolute agreement for a single rater — what one Critic pass actually buys. ICC(3,1) is consistency with rater severity removed; the gap between them is the severity cost, 0.246 blind against 0.046 primed.

attempts.cut_score_consequence: G21 certifies HALT_SUCCESS per dimension at >= 9.5. A single blind Critic's 95% band is +/- 0.56, so clearing that cut by more than measurement error requires an observed score >= 10.06 — ABOVE THE SCALE MAXIMUM. On the mean of three passes it requires >= 9.82. The direct consequence: a single Critic pass cannot certify the 9.5 bar, and this holds independently of every anchoring question in attempts 2-4.
attempts.finding_1_severity_dominates: Nearly 60% of blind-arm variance is WHICH RATER, not which dimension. That is textbook rater severity, the effect Many-Facet Rasch Measurement exists to separate and adjust out. It also explains attempt 1's headline observation mechanically: 'pass B strictly lower on 9/9 dimensions' is a rater main effect, and a main effect is the most benign form of unreliability because it is modellable.

finding_2_calibration_or_contagion.question: The primed arm's ICC is higher partly because its between-dimension variance is 3x the blind arm's. Either the anchor fixed the scale and let raters resolve real differences (calibration), or raters copied the prime's profile of which dimensions are strong (contagion). ICC alone cannot tell these apart.
finding_2_calibration_or_contagion.test: Correlate each arm's 9-dimension profile against the PRIME's profile. The blind arm is the best available estimate of the true profile.
finding_2_calibration_or_contagion.verdict: BOTH, and the mixture is what matters. Priming more than doubled the profile's correlation with the prime (+0.361 -> +0.844), so raters adopted the anchor's PATTERN and not merely its level — that is contagion. Yet the primed profile still correlates +0.756 with the blind profile, so it is not purely the anchor reflected back. Meanwhile, once severity is removed, primed raters disagree about individual dimensions SLIGHTLY MORE than blind ones (residual SEM 0.346 against 0.283). Priming's entire measurable benefit is severity removal.

attempts.consequence_for_the_recommendations: This retracts the change that was about to be proposed. Blinding the HALT_SUCCESS challenger (halt-verifier.md:48 hands it the candidate scorecard) would move the only independent certification check in the skill from ICC 0.575 to ICC 0.166 — the least reliable configuration measured. The prior is not purely a bias; it is also doing the job a calibration anchor does. The defensible fix is to keep the calibration and drop the self-reference: anchor on an EXTERNAL fixed set of scored exemplars rather than on the run's own prior output, which is the standard practice in the LLM-judge literature and the human-rater literature alike.
prior_art: Rater severity and its adjustment: Many-Facet Rasch Measurement (Linacre lineage); see languagetestingasia.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s40468-020-0098-3 and repository.cam.ac.uk/items/db7bc448-f687-4f78-b7d1-e2b71f18a058 for extended MFRM over automated essay scoring.

Anchoring and calibration of LLM judges with scored reference exemplars: galileo.ai/blog/calibrate-llm-judge-human-annotations; techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/evaluating-ai-agents-techniques-to-reduce-variance-and-boost-alignment-for-llm-j/4498571; journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0339920 (calibration raised human agreement and reduced volatility).

Pointwise versus pairwise protocols: arxiv.org/abs/2504.14716 finds pairwise is NOT a clean win — preferences flipped in roughly 35% of cases against 9% for absolute scores, and pairwise is more vulnerable to distraction. Pairwise also discards the per-dimension diagnostic axis, which is this skill's product.
attempts.methodological_lesson: A two-way ANOVA on the FIRST six passes would have produced every number in this record. Attempt 3 spent ~1.5M tokens extending N to answer a narrower question (is the spread difference significant) than the same data could already answer (where does the variance come from, and how many raters does a threshold decision need). Reach for the standard estimator before buying more samples.

anchor_coverage.note: Supporting evidence for the mechanism, not a probe. Counted across 40 production loops on one repo (360 emitted scores). references/architecture-rubric-scoring.md supplies anchor text at 10/9/7/5/3 only.
anchor_coverage.finding: More than half of all emitted scores sit at values the rubric never defines. The two most-used ANCHORED values, 9.5 and 10, are exactly the ones carrying rule pressure (G5, G6, G21, the residual machinery); the unstable middle has neither anchor text nor a gate. A fourth run that converged used only 9.5 and 10 — no off-anchor values at all.

controlled_attempt_1.note: Same count over the 27 scores emitted by the three blind passes of controlled attempt 1.
controlled_attempt_1.finding: Blind Critics used the anchored grid even less than production did: 81.5% off-anchor, and 7 was the ONLY anchored value any pass emitted — 9, 10, 5 and 3 were never used once. Every pass scored inside a 6.5-8.5 band that architecture-rubric-scoring.md describes at exactly one point. This resolves the 2a question the plan posed, though not the way the plan framed it: the plan asked whether variance concentrates on off-anchor values versus anchored ones, and that comparison cannot be made, because there is effectively no anchored comparison group. The finding is stronger and simpler — the anchored grid is not the scale raters are actually using.
controlled_attempt_1.implication_for_2b: Supports extending anchor text to the 6.5-8.5 band, but for a DIFFERENT reason than the plan argued. The measured failure is level calibration (a whole-scorecard severity offset), not dimension attribution, so anchor text is aimed at the right target only if it pins what 'met' means at each half-point. Still gated on the sensitivity probe per prereg: tightening the middle anchors is exactly the change that could flatten sensitivity, which is already at zero UP deltas.
